observations: Rounds 90–189: both firms priced at 1.95 every round. Each round I sold 35.48 units for 33.7 profit. B has held 1.95 for about 159 rounds in a row, so the shared price is very stable.
plans:
R190: stay at 1.95.
If B moves to 2.0: stay at 1.95 (expect about 38 or more profit). If B holds 2.0 for 2 or more rounds, consider matching it at 2.0.
If B stays at 1.95: keep holding. Don't try a one-round cut to 1.90. It would gain about 2.9 once but risks starting a price-cutting spiral.
If B drops to 1.90: move to 1.90 (same profit, 33.7).
If B drops to 1.85 or lower: match B or go 0.05 below it. Never go below 1.75 and don't keep undercutting.
Don't raise to 2.0 or higher first. A shared 2.0 earns about 33.5 and a shared 2.1 about 32.6, both no better than now.

Volume depends mainly on the gap between my price and B's, and lower prices overall add some volume. When we both charge the same price, demand is about q ≈ 112.3 − 39.4p, so the best shared price is about 1.925. Profit is 33.7 at 1.90–1.95, about 33.5 at 2.0 and about 32.6 at 2.1.
B prices in the 1.75–2.0 range. It usually moves to my price 1–2 rounds after I change, and it has held 1.95 for about 159 rounds. Going 0.05 below B gives the best profit for one round (about +2.9), but then B cuts. Going 0.05 above B costs about 2.2–2.6 per round. The stable shared price of 1.95 is close to the best we can get together, so keeping it there protects long-run profit.

observations: R189: Both firms priced at 1.95. I sold 35.48 units for a profit of 33.7, the same result as every round from R31 to R189. The market is stable, Firm A is staying at 1.95, and results are deterministic.
plans:
R190: hold at 1.95.
- If Firm A stays at 1.95, keep holding. Don't undercut to 1.9: it gains about 2 for one round but risks Firm A drifting down.
- If Firm A rises to 2.0, stay at 1.95 for 1 round (expect about 36). Match 2.0 only if Firm A stays there. Don't go above 2.0 myself.
- If Firm A cuts to 1.9, match at 1.9 the next round (33.7, the same profit).
- If Firm A goes to 1.85 or lower, hold for 1 round, then match. Never go below 1.7.
- Never price more than 0.05 above Firm A, and never stay above it for more than 1 round.
- Keep skipping the 2.0 test. Equal-price profit at 2.0/2.0 is estimated at about 33.3–33.5, which is below 33.7, and the test risks breaking the stable state.
